en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Twelve Mudrās and One Hundred and Eight Names of the Immaculate Great Auspicious Goddess,
translated by [the monk] holding the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sisi, Teci, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Duke of Su.

The Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Tripitaka Master of Daixingshan Monastery, who was granted a fief of three thousand households, invested with the rank of Purple Robe, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and bestowed the title of Great Mirror of Wisdom, translated this by imperial decree: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the world of Sukhāvatī,
together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas.
Namely, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta,
and the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva,
Samantaprabhāsa Bodhisattva,
and Gaganagañja Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Dispeller of All Fears,
the Bodhisattva Holder of All Pure Auspiciousness,
and the Bodhisattva Holder of All Meritorious Marks.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas, with the Bodhisattva Holding the Sun and Moon of the Three Times and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī as their leaders, were present.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara went to where the World-Honored One was,
prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the Great Goddess Śrī also went to where the Buddha was and prostrated with her head at the Buddha’s feet.

They circumambulated [the Buddha] for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of times and, having paid homage to all the bodhisattvas dwelling in the world of Peace and Bliss (*Anomala*), withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One beheld the goddess Śrī.
Adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of merits,
surrounded by koṭis of Tathāgatas,
and praised and extolled by all the Śakras, Brahmās, and World-Protectors.
With a great Brahma-voice, he addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Avalokiteśvara, if there should be kings, princes, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, or śūdras..."

If the kṣatriya king and all sentient beings within his realm uphold this "Stainless Praise of the Twelve Mudrās and One Hundred and Eight Names of the Great Auspicious Goddess," [they shall obtain these benefits].
All fears and afflictions shall be entirely eliminated;
no harm shall come from the terrors of all enemies, whether human or non-human;
and all wealth and grain shall be abundant and plentiful.
The auspicious goddess Śrī always dwells within the residence of that Kṣatriya king.
At that time, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent, World-Honored One! You have spoken these words most wonderfully."
If there are those who hold the name of the goddess Śrī,
they shall obtain such benefits and merit.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Fearless One, [spoke thus].
He then addressed the Buddha, saying, “World-Honored One,
in what place did the goddess Śrī plant roots of goodness?
The Buddha said, “She planted them in the presence of Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.”
Planting roots of merit.
O fearless Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, I recall that in a past life,
in the world-realm Ratnasambhava...
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Śrī-golden-light-śrī, who is a mountain of vaidūrya gold and an ocean of merit from precious flowers,
appeared in the world;
it was there that the Great Goddess Śrī planted roots of virtue.
Furthermore, at the abodes of many other Tathāgatas,
this Great Goddess Śrī has cultivated roots of merit through the recitation of such names of the Tathāgatas.
These Tathāgatas constantly follow the Great Auspicious Goddess (Mahāśrī-devī),
who is able to liberate one from all transgressions and extinguish all afflictions.
It causes all bodies to become stainless;
it summons and increases all wealth and grain,
and is able to eliminate poverty.
It is able to summon all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas;
it is able to pacify all oppression, affliction, disputes, litigation, and warfare.
Able to accomplish the six pāramitās, namely:

If there are those who respectfully receive, uphold, read, and recite it,
those sons and daughters of good family will generate a vast accumulation of merit.
All the Tathāgatas bestow this prophecy upon the Great Auspicious Goddess:
"In the world-system called Auspicious Jewel Adornment, you shall attain equal and perfect enlightenment,
and your name shall be Auspicious Maṇi-Jewel-Born Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
That world is adorned with various kinds of celestial jewels; in that world,
only this Tathāgata produces light.
In that Buddha-world, the assembly of bodhisattvas possesses natural radiance and immeasurable lifespan;
from the void, the sounds of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha are produced.
All bodhisattvas who are born in that Buddha-world are all miraculously born upon lotus thrones. What, then,
are the twelve chapters of the one hundred and eight names of the Immaculate Praise?
Fearless Avalokiteśvara, listen attentively now.

This Great Auspicious Mantra and its one hundred and eight names are able to eliminate all afflictions and destroy all transgressions.
It is able to summon all blessings;
it is able to eliminate all inauspiciousness;
it is able to summon all merit and virtue.
If there are those who uphold, read, and recite the names of the Tathāgatas,
they should rise early and make offerings of incense and flowers to all the Buddhas.
For the sake of the goddess Śrī,
one should burn sandalwood incense and recite this sutra.
Before long, that person will obtain all auspiciousness, all peace and happiness, and joy.
All devas shall protect them, and all their undertakings shall be fully accomplished.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and the Great Goddess Śrī Mahādevī [arose from their seats].
When the entire great assembly heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all filled with great joy; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
This concludes the *Mahāmaṅgaladevī-dvādaśamudrā-aṣṭottaraśatanāma-vimala-mahāyāna-sūtra*. Great Auspiciousness.
The Sutra of the Twelve Mudrās and One Hundred and Eight Names of the Stainless Mahāyāna Goddess of Heaven. Oṃ.
